newsitem.title: USA: IBM says currency cut Q4 EPS by $0.18/shr.
newsitem.headline: IBM says currency cut Q4 EPS by $0.18/shr.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp Chief Financial Officer G. Richard Thoman on Tuesday said currency fluctuations in the fourth quarter had a negative impact on earnings of about $0.18 a share.

Thoman, in a meeting with Wall Street analysts on Tuesday, said he felt "pretty good" about the company's performance in 1997. Issues facing the company included memory chip pricing and a shifting mix to lower-margin products, he said. Currency changes remained a "wild card."
Thoman said IBM's nine percent revenue growth, in constant currency, was the best since the company's "hey day" in 1985.

"I feel pretty good about 1997 as I stand here today," Thoman told analysts. "We face what appears to be a pretty strong product demand for all our product lines....We face some specific issues in DRAMs (dynamic random access memory chips) and currency is a wild card."

Thoman said that IBM did not spend as much on restructuring as previously planned. He said the company in the fourth quarter spent $200 million on restructuring, versus estimates of $300 million to $400 million.
IBM no longer writes down as a restructuring charge the money it spends to cover employee buyout plans.
